Q1.answer: The person is not defined: the brief and document do not say who they are or whether requests come through a UI, command or API. The controller does check the gate before accepting a move and refuses, naming the unmet condition, if the gate is not met, a rollback is running or blocked, or another move is pending.

Q2.answer: The rollout controller is the only component that writes billing_mode and the rollout record, but where it runs and what hosts it are not defined. Its triggers are a person's move, rollback, resume or abort request, the nightly comparison results, and a restart after a crash; how the auto-trigger from the charge failure monitor reaches it is also not defined.

Q3.answer: A day is clean only if the comparison job completed for that day, at least one invoice was compared, and mismatches divided by invoices compared is under 0.1%. The one-cent rule decides which invoices count as mismatches, and the rate uses only those counts; unresolved mismatches are not in the clean-day test and block the move at move time instead, though whether they should also make a day unclean is an unconfirmed assumption.

Q4.answer: Both engines read billing_mode fresh before every charge attempt and ledger write, with no caching, and the flag is not written during R1 to R5 except at the flip. What stops a double charge at the switch is the per-(customer, billing period) claim check in the billing ledger, which applies regardless of the flag value.

Q5.answer: A charge claim is one ledger row per (customer, billing period) per attempt, with an idempotency key from customer, period and attempt number. The engine that is about to charge creates it before calling the provider, as a conditional create that fails if a successful or pending claim already exists, and its states are pending, successful and failed.

Q6.answer: Once R1 sets the freeze marker, each engine checks it before each new claim and, while it is set, queues due charges instead of creating claims. In-flight claims are resolved by querying the provider with their idempotency keys, and a timeout leaves the claim pending. R1 has no time limit or retry limit yet, so it stays running and shows the pending claim count until those are set.

Q7.answer: Due means the invoice total is above zero and there is no successful claim for the period. For origin shadow the amount comes from the old engine's ledger invoice, and for origin both it comes from the shadow-store invoice, in each case as pinned at the R2 snapshot; for origin new_only it is the final invoice from R3.

Q8.answer: The alert goes on the same channel used for auto-rollback triggers, but that channel is not named, and the escalation path beyond on-call is not defined. On-call decides to abort, and does so by sending an abort request through the controller.

Q9.answer: The flag stays at the origin through the whole rollback and changes only once, at the flip, where it is set to old_only. An abort does not write the flag at all: it sets the rollout mode in the rollout record back to the origin, and billing_mode still holds the origin.

Q10.answer: A period is closed if its end time is at or before the R2 snapshot time, and the controller decides this by comparing against that snapshot. Closed periods are settled in R4 at the pinned amount, while open periods are queued and charged by normal processing after the flip; whether the current system has a billing close job is unconfirmed.

Q11.answer: In scope means every (customer, billing period) that has an invoice from either engine, or usage events, since the rollout entered shadow. R4 and R5 act only on the closed periods in that set, and how in-scope tracking behaves after a reset is still open.

Q12.answer: The charge failure monitor measures the new engine's resolved charge attempts in each rolling 10-minute window, counting provider declines, timeouts resolved as not charged, and engine errors on a charge attempt, and excluding claim-check refusals and queued items. In both and new_only only the new engine charges, so only its attempts count. The mechanism by which the controller learns the monitor tripped and the minimum attempt count per window are not defined.

Q13.answer: The rollback job is the old engine's code run by the controller, and it reads the origin and the current step from the rollout record, never from billing_mode. For origin new_only the controller starts the rollback job to run R3 and R4, but the process that hosts it is not defined.

Q14.answer: The queue is the set of ledger rows with status queued, and each stores the customer, period, amount due and source invoice. Engines add to it when a charge is blocked by a freeze, a failed claim create or an unreadable flag, and the old engine or normal processing takes from it after the flip or an abort. On abort to shadow, rows whose period has a successful claim are dropped, the rest go to the old engine, and open periods wait for normal processing; the drain order is still undefined.

Q15.answer: On-call sends a resume command to the controller naming the blocked step, and the controller re-checks that step's precondition and re-runs that whole step, not just the part that failed, without re-running earlier steps. The transport for the command is not defined.

Q16.answer: Engines read the flag fresh before every charge attempt and ledger write, with no caching. If a worker cannot read it, it does not charge, writes each due charge to the queue with no claim and its amount, raises an alert and retries the read on its next cycle, and drains the queue once a read succeeds; the drain order is not defined.

Q17.answer: No, the document does not stop it. The freeze check and the claim create are not made atomic, so a late claim is possible, and the only check against it is that R2 refuses to start while any claim is pending.

Q18.answer: R4 charges the invoice version pinned at the R2 snapshot: the shadow-store invoice for origin both and the ledger invoice for origin shadow. Invoices that change after the snapshot do not change the R4 amount, so the amount is as fresh as the snapshot time.

Q19.answer: The premise is not quite right: queued rows do store an amount due and the source invoice reference, so the drain uses that stored amount. The old engine re-checks its current invoice for that period, and if it differs from the stored amount by more than one cent the row is not charged, the period is marked for on-call, and the drain continues.

Q20.answer: The recorded state is the last persisted flip step, and on restart the controller re-runs the remaining steps from the record. The flag is written first and the freeze marker is cleared after it, so a crash after the flag write leaves the freeze set and nothing charges; the queue drain and gate reset are safe to repeat because of the claim checks and stored amounts.

Q21.answer: On restart the controller reads the pending move and compares billing_mode with its target. If the flag already holds the target it marks the move done without rewriting the flag, and it does not recheck the gate, because the move was accepted before the crash.

Q22.answer: A rollback request names the person and is sent to the controller, which records it, but the transport and exact content of the request are not defined, and the auto-trigger path to the controller is also undefined. If a forward move is pending, the rollback is still accepted: the controller first clears the pending move, then reads billing_mode and records it as the origin.

Q23.answer: The old engine is the normal billing worker, which is stopped in new_only, while the rollback job is the old engine code the controller runs for the current rollback step, separate from normal work. The controller starts the rollback job for R3 and R4 when origin is new_only, but the process that hosts it is not defined.

Q24.answer: A ledger invoice is data holding the old engine's computed total for one customer and period, and a charge is a provider action against a claim, so one period can have one successful charge and many invoices over time. R5 checks that the old engine's current invoice total matches the successful charges for that period in the ledger within one cent, and in shadow the nightly comparison pairs the shadow-store new-engine invoices with the old engine's ledger invoices.

q7.answer: Workers learn of a mode change only by reading billing_mode fresh before each charge attempt and ledger write, since nothing is pushed to them. The document does not say what happens to an invoice already mid-computation at that moment, beyond the claim check and freeze marker that prevent a double charge.

q8.answer: The evidence is kept in the shadow store as one nightly comparison result per day, which the controller reads to update the gate counters in the rollout record. The controller refuses any forward move whose gate is not met, but the structure of the gate counters is not yet defined.

q9.answer: The charge failure monitor detects the auto-rollback condition by measuring the new engine's charge failure rate in rolling 10-minute windows. When the rate is above 2 percent in both or new_only, it is meant to start the rollback automatically, but how the controller learns of the trip and the minimum attempt count per window are not defined.

q10.answer: During a rollback, charges that fall due are queued with their amount and invoice reference and no claim is created while the freeze marker is set. Closed periods are charged in R4 by the rollback job at their pinned amounts if they are still due, and everything queued is drained through the old engine after the flip under the normal claim checks, while open periods wait for normal processing after the flip.

q11.answer: The conditional claim create stops it: a new claim for a (customer, billing period) fails if a successful or pending claim already exists, and R4 skips any period that already has a successful claim. This holds whatever the flag or a stale read says, so a late claim cannot produce a second successful charge.

q12.answer: The rollout record keeps the last completed step, and a failed step moves the rollback to blocked_rollback with the step and reason recorded and an alert sent, while billing_mode stays at the origin and the freeze marker stays set. On-call then resumes by re-running the blocked step or aborts back to the origin, and a crash resumes from the last persisted step; the resume transport is not defined.
